extracted.intended_audience: legislators, political reformers, and political theorists designing suffrage and representation systems
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidelines and practical conditions for constructing a representative democracy and suffrage rules that (a) allow instructed minorities influence, (b) avoid class ascendancy and collective mediocrity, and (c) specify who should be qualified or disqualified to vote and under what tests or weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of all (personal representation) rather than only majority
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative government should be 'representative of all, and not solely of the majority' so that interests, opinions, and grades of intellect which are outnumbered are nevertheless heard and can obtain influence proportioned to their numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a system (e.g., Mr. Hare's personal representation) that enables minorities — especially the 'instructed minority' scattered through constituencies — to unite and return representatives proportionate to their numbers, thereby allowing them to be present in the assembly and exert moral and intellectual influence beyond mere headcount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent collective mediocrity by ensuring the presence of superior minds
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural tendency of representative government is towards collective mediocrity; constitutions should ensure superior intellects and characters are heard rather than silenced by local majorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design electoral mechanisms that make it feasible for highly cultivated individuals to obtain seats (so assemblies include 'a few of the first minds'), since their presence elevates general deliberation and can produce occasional great leaders (e.g., 'Pericles').

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an institutional function of Antagonism (point d'appui) to check dominant power
rubrics_metrics.description: Government requires a stable organ of opposition — a 'point d'appui' — to prevent any single power from becoming sole and to drive continual improvement through rival influences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A representation system should supply an institutional rallying point for dissenting opinions (the instructed minority acting within Parliament) so that rival powers persist and prevent stagnation and decay of the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation should represent persons not merely geographic units
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament must represent human beings rather than 'artificial units' like towns and counties; localities are represented when their human inhabitants are properly represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid electoral rules that treat towns/counties as having rights separate from their inhabitants; permit individuals to be classified by feelings or interests other than geography (so local character is not the sole principle of political classification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal access to the franchise except for narrowly justified temporary exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The electoral privilege should be open to all persons of full age who desire to obtain it; peremptory exclusion of any portion of citizens is unacceptable except for limited, positively-justified reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the suffrage broadly accessible; any exclusion should be temporary, required by positive reasons, and of a kind that all can reasonably fulfill (not permanent class exclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum literacy and numeracy as a suffrage condition
rubrics_metrics.description: No person should participate in the suffrage without being able to read, write, and perform the common operations of arithmetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require a simple, public test at registry (e.g., copy a sentence from an English book and perform a 'rule of three' sum in the registrar's presence) with fixed rules and publicity to prevent fraud; these basic skills are prerequisites for intelligent use of the franchise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal education must precede universal enfranchisement (policy precondition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If society has neglected to provide elementary instruction to all, universal teaching must precede universal enfranchisement; otherwise there is a hardship in conferring the vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the duty to make elementary education accessible (gratuitously or affordably) so that literacy/numeracy requirements do not unfairly exclude the poor; political expansion should be accompanied by improvements in education infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax-paying requirement for electors of tax-levying assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: The assembly which votes the taxes, either general or local, should be elected exclusively by those who pay something towards the taxes imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because those who pay nothing have motive to be lavish with others' money, representation should be coextensive with taxation. Consider mechanisms so taxation is visible to electors — e.g., direct capitation tax, rating electors to assessed taxes, or a small annual payment from registered electors tied to national expenditure — so every elector feels a direct stake in public spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualify recipients of parish relief (and similar dependents) for a fixed term
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of parish relief should be a peremptory disqualification for the franchise; e.g., require that an applicant's name has not been on parish books as a relief recipient for a fixed term (suggested five years) prior to registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat dependence on eleemosynary support as justifying temporary disqualification because such persons 'bring nothing, or less than he takes away' to common concerns; make these exclusions non-permanent and removable on restoration of normal self-sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualify uncertificated bankrupts or recent insolvents until recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: An uncertificated bankrupt, or one who has taken the benefit of insolvency law, should be disqualified from the franchise until the person has paid debts or proven they are not, and have not long been, dependent on charity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make insolvency-based disqualifications conditional and temporary: restore franchise upon demonstrated financial rehabilitation or evidence of non-dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-payment of taxes as a continuing disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-payment of taxes, when long persisted and not from inadvertence, should disqualify for the franchise while the non-payment lasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tax compliance as a basis for maintaining the link between representation and contribution; allow for remedies and restoration when obligations are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject property as a basis for assigning greater voting influence
rubrics_metrics.description: It is 'entirely inadmissible' that superiority of influence be conferred in consideration of property — property is an imperfect and odious criterion for plurality of votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid connecting plurality of votes with pecuniary qualification, as this will be 'supremely odious' and politically impracticable; prefer non-pecuniary measures of individual superiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign extra voting weight on grounds of individual mental superiority (education/occupation), not property
rubrics_metrics.description: The only justification for reckoning one person's opinion as equivalent to more than one is individual mental superiority; in absence of a national education system, the nature and successful performance of one's occupation can be an approximate test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow two or more votes for those who exercise superior functions (e.g., employers of labor, foremen, skilled tradesmen, bankers, merchants, manufacturers) provided occupation has been persevered in for a reasonable duration (suggested three years) to avoid nominal claims; grant plurality to liberal professions and graduates where serious educational tests/examinations exist and are fairly open to all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural voting for university graduates and professionally examined persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of professions requiring serious conditions of education or those holding university degrees could be accorded plurality of votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admit graduates and those with satisfactory certificates from legitimate higher-branch schools to multiple votes, with safeguards ensuring the teaching and examinations are real and open to fair competition (example: 'local' or 'middle class' examinations at Oxford).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep suffrage tests simple and publicly administered to avoid fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: While more extensive knowledge (history, geography, institutions) would be desirable as suffrage tests, they are often inaccessible and would invite partiality and fraud; better to use very simple tests for now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid complex educational tests until trustworthy, national systems or fair examination machinery exist. Use simple, transparent literacy/numeracy tests administered publicly to registrars to prevent 'partiality, chicanery, and every kind of fraud.'
